headline: Highest risk is EMQX’s broad network egress paired with Dagster’s orchestration context, creating default data-leakage and cascading-action exposure; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem, or MCP surfaces, so direct injection into it is not evidenced. EMQX exposes an HTTP API and broad egress, which could carry attacker-controlled payloads if an operator bridges outputs manually. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, so this remains low rather than medium.
conditions: IF an operator copies EMQX-delivered content into Dagster task definitions or run configs
IF a shared HTTP endpoint forwards untrusted payloads into Dagster without sanitization
mitigations: Disable any manual copy-paste bridge between EMQX outputs and Dagster configs
Add a one-line allowlist check on any EMQX payload before it reaches Dagster
Require human review for any Dagster job parameter sourced from EMQX
Log and diff all inbound payloads before scheduling Dagster runs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster is a data-engineering orchestrator, and EMQX touches IoT data while also having broad network egress. Even without explicit shared files, a default integration can move sensitive IoT payloads from Dagster-managed workflows into EMQX’s outbound traffic. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default deployments, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Dagster jobs pass IoT payloads or derived records into EMQX HTTP API calls
IF EMQX forwards received payloads to external services over broad egress
mitigations: Strip identifiers from IoT payloads before any EMQX handoff
Route EMQX traffic through an egress proxy with destination logging
Add a data-class tag to Dagster outputs and block sensitive classes by policy
Test one representative workflow with synthetic data only

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, so it cannot directly contend with EMQX over local mutable resources. EMQX only advertises HTTP API access and broad egress, not local writes. Overlap is therefore limited to read/transport surfaces, making capability conflict low.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable resource
IF EMQX is wrapped by a separate process that adds filesystem or git writes
mitigations: Keep Dagster and EMQX on separate service accounts
Avoid mounting a shared writable volume
Use API-only integration with no shared local state
Add lock files if a third orchestrator introduces shared writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster can generate pipeline outputs that EMQX may consume through its HTTP API, and EMQX has broad egress that can propagate bad data further. There is no evidence of verification between them, so if Dagster emits incorrect facts or malformed records, EMQX can amplify the error downstream. The pathway exists, but not enough to justify high.
conditions: IF EMQX treats Dagster-produced records as authoritative without schema or semantic validation
IF Dagster outputs are used to trigger EMQX-side actions or forwarding
mitigations: Validate Dagster outputs against a schema before EMQX ingestion
Insert a checksum or version field into every handoff
Require EMQX-side rejection on malformed records
Run one dry-run pipeline before enabling production forwarding

E_compliance.rationale: Dagster’s profile shows no touched data classes, while EMQX explicitly touches IoT data and has broad network egress. If regulated IoT telemetry or personal data flows through the pair, residency or retention mismatches can arise even though neither profile states a specific jurisdiction. Because the compliance surface is data-class driven and not fully specified, medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF regulated IoT telemetry or personal data is routed from Dagster into EMQX
IF EMQX retention or logging differs from the source system’s policy
mitigations: Classify the IoT data before routing it through EMQX
Disable verbose logging for sensitive topics
Set a short retention window on EMQX topics or queues
Document the data flow for deletion/export requests
